headlines.text: Zinedine Zidane named new France head coach following World Cup. Ex-France superstar player Zinedine Zidane unveiled as new head coach following team's World Cup 2026 disappointment.
Netanyahu in the White House: What’s on the agenda and what’s next?. The Israeli PM's visit to the US comes amid raids in the occupied West Bank, before the October 27 elections.

Sixty Palestinians detained by Israel return to Gaza, describe abuses. The freed men, some in wheelchairs, describe horrific abuses in Israeli detention.

Malaysia detains more than 100 Rohingya seeking help from the UN. Malaysian police have detained more than 100 Rohingya refugees and asylum seekers who were seeking help from the UN.
Trump calls protester ‘communist’ after Michigan speech interruption. A protester was removed after interrupting US President Donald Trump’s remarks at a Michigan auto event.

Brian Harman flips the bird after 3M Open finish, gets a laugh from Scottie Scheffler. Brian Harman raised his middle finger at a TV camera in the scoring area as Scottie Scheffler erupted in laughter and a fist pump at the 3M Open.

RFK Jr says Fauci prioritized 'getting on TV' over public health after revealing diary release. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. says Anthony Fauci's diary entries reveal a fixation on fame, claiming the doctor did incalculable damage to public health trust.

Kelsey Grammer admits it's 'exhausting' when movies try to alter history to fit modern tastes. "Frasier" star Kelsey Grammer told Katie Miller that Hollywood keeps flopping by forcing modern spins on classic stories that ought to respect history and culture.

NY Times reporter admits Trump's 'delusional' foes have wrongly written his political obituary many times. New York Times reporter Jonathan Swan said President Donald Trump showed him a document comparing himself to Napoleon, Stalin, and Genghis Khan in terms of power.

White House fires back after John Mellencamp mocks Trump's Gulf of America during concert. John Mellencamp paused his "Pink Houses" performance to mock Trump's Gulf of America executive order, prompting a sharp White House response.

Trump's $15B lawsuit against The New York Times carries on as judge gives his attorneys chance to amend filing. President Trump celebrates after a judge allows his legal team to amend the massive $15 billion defamation lawsuit against The New York Times by August 27.

19 cadets rushed to hospitals after mystery illness strikes military-style youth academy in DC area. A mass casualty response was launched at a Maryland National Guard youth academy after cadets reported dizziness, headaches and nausea on Sunday.

'Baywatch' star Brooks Nader suffers wardrobe malfunction during Saint-Tropez getaway. Brooks Nader's leopard-print playsuit slipped during a Saint-Tropez beach day at Club 55, adding to her history of viral wardrobe malfunctions.

Pro Bowl player requests trade from Tampa Bay Buccaneers on eve of training camp amid contract dispute. Vita Vea's trade request comes as the Pro Bowl nose tackle ranks 19th in pay among interior linemen despite anchoring Tampa Bay's top-ranked run defense.

WNBA love feud explodes as NaLyssa Smith fires back at DiJonai Carrington's cheating claims. NaLyssa Smith went live on Twitch to address DiJonai Carrington's cheating allegations, questioning why the Chicago Sky guard aired their breakup publicly.

Netflix exec claims ketamine confession in ‘trust exercise’ cost him $1.1M job: lawsuit. Kevin Baillie says he shared his medically supervised ketamine therapy for depression during a vulnerability exercise at a Netflix workplace retreat.

With wildfires raging in France and Spain, fire crews race against next heat wave. French President Emmanuel Macron said France was "facing a completely unprecedented fire," describing the situation as France's worst fire-related crisis since World War II.

Platner energized Maine's Democrats. Jackson's challenge will be to keep them engaged. Democrats have a new candidate for U.S. Senate in Maine: Troy Jackson. In one of the country's most closely-watched races, he'll have less than 100 days to make his case.

Authors have mixed feelings about the $1.5B Anthropic copyright infringement ruling. Some say the $3,100 per title payout is small compensation for what they view as big, ongoing threats from the makers of generative AI models.

Inside Joe Manchin's new quest to elect more Independents to Congress. The former West Virginia senator was a lifelong Democrat before deciding to register as an independent two years ago. He now wants to create similar pathways for other politicians in both parties.

The 'cockroach' in the machine: How Gen Z is rattling South Asia's elites. South Asia's leaders have long boasted about their demographic dividend. But the region's young people are turning it into a political reckoning.

3 dead in mass shooting in Seattle. And, U.S. and Iran pause fighting. A mass shooting at a Seattle festival has left three people dead. And, the U.S. and Iran have been exchanging diplomatic messages after nearly tw weeks of intense fighting.

France continues to fight devastating wildfires, while progress is made in Spain. In southern France, a wildfire in the region of Gironde is still active, while two major fires in central Spain are finally coming under control, ahead of the fourth heat wave of the summer.

Baltimore will turn 911 into more than just an emergency number. Baltimore is rethinking what it means to call 911, and who responds. Callers who don't need police will get help finding social services and healthcare before they actually fall into crisis.

Kalshi attacks a Wisconsin law banning election bets as 'voter suppression'. The spat between the leading prediction market company and a key battleground state could be a glimpse into the next major fight between states and the fast-growing industry.
